description: A @spec naming a type fz doesn't know (e.g. @spec f(non_neg_integer) :: integer) prints error[resolve/type-alias]: compiler2 could not resolve function contract for f: unknown type name non_neg_integer, located at <generated>, and then the program runs anyway and exits 0 (verified on interp and run, c652387c8). An error must stop the program with a non-zero status and point at the spec's source line. Whether non_neg_integer, pos_integer and no_return should exist as type names is a separate question; record it here or in its own ticket. Found by the fz-sc8.7 builder.
title: A spec naming an unknown type stops the program and points at the spec
